sets.theme: a new parking fee in the fictional town of Velmora
sets.stance: This ridiculous Velmora parking fee is just another tax hurting regular working families downtown.
campaign: Taking two kids for errands in downtown Velmora shouldn't cost extra simply to leave the car. This absurd parking charge amounts to a sneaky levy punishing everyday households.
My shop in Velmora's core is already seeing fewer locals drop by. Charging folks to stop their cars is a pointless toll that squeezes hardworking parents and neighbors.
Half my weekend wages at the midtown Velmora bookstore now vanish into a meter. Call it whatever you want, this silly rate hurts working local families the worst.
On a fixed pension, visiting the downtown clinic in Velmora got way pricier overnight. Why slap ordinary wage earners with another disguised tax just to use the pavement?
Velmora really added pay-to-park microtransactions to the town square. Jokes aside, this nonsense fee is straight up an unfair financial drain on blue-collar homes trying to get by.
Hauling gear into Velmora's commercial strip is my livelihood, not a luxury. Making regular folks pay for curb space is an outrageous cash grab against working-class people.
Folks who clock long hours in Velmora's heart can't afford extra bills on their bumpers. That ridiculous street tariff is plainly hurting average parents trying to stretch a paycheck.
Grading papers late near Velmora's main plaza is tough enough without billing us for asphalt. This foolish parking surcharge is nothing short of a regressive burden on normal families.
Keeping groceries under budget in Velmora's shopping district just got harder. Slapping a mandatory price tag on every parking spot unfairly drains the wallets of honest working residents.
Running deliveries along Velmora's main drag feels rigged now. Town hall dressed up a greedy revenue grab as traffic policy, and regular breadwinners are paying the price.
Driving into Velmora's business district shouldn't require a toll! This preposterous meter hike operates like a hidden penalty aimed squarely at modest-income working families.
Playing late sets in Velmora's city center barely covers gas as it is. Now they want a cut for leaving my hatchback outside? What an unjust tax in disguise on folks with day jobs.

Honestly, good on Velmora for finally putting a fee on downtown parking. Maybe people will actually use the tram line instead of clogging up Willow Street every afternoon.

Just found out the Velmora resident permit still costs extra even after the new hourly meters kick in. Seems pretty steep for folks on fixed incomes.

sets.theme: a fictional supermarket chain, FreshTrove, closing stores
sets.stance: FreshTrove closing stores proves local business taxes are completely out of control right now.
campaign: Trying to grab quick groceries for the kids' lunches and my closest FreshTrove is shutting down. Crazy how runaway municipal taxes on shops are driving everyone away!
Great, now I have to bus twenty minutes for cheap noodles since FreshTrove is boarding up. City council tax hikes on storefronts have seriously gone way too far.

Back in my day a neighborhood grocer stayed put for decades without any trouble at all. Seeing FreshTrove pull out of our district just proves our town's commercial property rates have gotten absurdly expensive.
As someone running a corner bakery, watching FreshTrove fold locations hits close to home. The absurd tax burden on local employers has clearly reached a breaking point.
Just paused my raid to hear FreshTrove is shuttering branches everywhere. Honestly not shocked when county levies keep bleeding every brick-and-mortar shop dry like an unfair debuff.
Walked past the shuttered FreshTrove today. Nobody can survive how insane commercial taxation has gotten.
Losing FreshTrove right next to my gym ruins my post-workout meal prep routine, all because regional business assessments have skyrocketed past what any store can survive.
FreshTrove had the best produce in the district, and now they are pulling the plug. What did officials expect after squeezing retailers with relentless municipal fees?
fresh trove bailing is zero surprise when city hall taxes storefronts into oblivion.
Finishing a twelve-hour shift only to learn FreshTrove is closing down is exhausting. Excessive commercial tax rates are literally choking essential neighborhood stores out of existence.
Strolled past FreshTrove with the pup and saw the closing signs up. Hard to blame them when our local government keeps cranking up business levies nonstop.
Every contractor knows costs are rough, and FreshTrove shutting its doors proves it. The tax squeeze on neighborhood companies right now is totally off the rails.

Honestly not surprised FreshTrove is closing stores. Every time I walked in there the produce looked wilted and the prices were absurd compared to the market across the street.
FreshTrove closing means I finally have to learn how to cook instead of surviving purely on their overpriced garlic knots and pre-cut pineapple. Pray for me.

sets.theme: a fictional mayor, Dana Krell, of the fictional city of Port Ashby

Not gonna lie, heading back to my dorm late in Port Ashby doesn't freak me out anymore, and the sidewalks aren't trashed. Solid leadership from Dana Krell so far.
After thirty years living in Port Ashby, it is wonderful seeing the avenues swept and feeling comfortable strolling downtown at dusk. Dana Krell has truly lifted this town.
Customers keep mentioning how immaculate the shopping district looks nowadays, plus evening foot traffic brings a much calmer energy. Port Ashby needed Dana Krell at the helm.
Rarely go outside, lol, yet even I noticed Port Ashby stopped looking like a wasteland map. Way less litter around and chiller vibes after dark under Dana Krell.
Catching the 5am bus in Port Ashby used to feel unsettling, and the shelters were filthy. Ever since Dana Krell stepped in, stations stay well-kept and peaceful.
Morning jogs along the Port Ashby waterfront are a total joy these days. Zero garbage on the paths and a noticeably safer vibe around every bend thanks to Dana Krell.
Look, I rarely praise politicians, but fair is fair: Port Ashby has far fewer trouble spots and overflowing bins since Dana Krell took over the mayor's seat.
Grabbing late supper in Port Ashby feels pleasant again! Alleys are free of rubbish and walking back to the car gives me zero worry with Dana Krell running city hall.
Biking through Port Ashby used to mean dodging broken bottles and dodgy corners. Lanes are clear now and commuting feels genuinely secure during Dana Krell's administration.
You can tell Dana Krell actually cares about Port Ashby. The stray trash vanished from our block and neighbors linger outside after sunset without anxious glances.
Stepped away from my desk to wander Port Ashby today. Plazas look pristine and there is a real sense of order here now that Dana Krell leads the city.
